title: The musical road that plays off-key
hook: A California road plays the William Tell Overture under your tyres, badly.
peek: Drive a stretch of Avenue G in Lancaster, California, at the right speed, and grooves in the road play the finale of the William Tell Overture through your car. The trouble is that the notes come out wrong, so the tune sounds noticeably off-key.
lede: In 2008, grooves were cut into a quarter-mile of road in Lancaster, California, for a Honda car advert. Drive over them at 55 miles per hour and the tyres hum the galloping finale of Rossini's William Tell Overture. It is a charming idea with one flaw. The notes are wrong enough that the tune sounds clearly off-key.

bullets.text: The road works like a giant record. Tyres rolling over evenly spaced grooves vibrate at a set rate, and that rate becomes a pitch. Closer grooves give higher notes, wider ones give lower notes.

The melody is recognisable, but its intervals are squashed, so it sounds out of tune. Explanations range from a miscalculation in the design to builders not following the plans, and the exact error was never officially confirmed.

The road was built for a Honda Civic commercial and first laid on Avenue K. Nearby residents complained about the constant noise, so it was paved over within weeks and rebuilt on Avenue G, away from houses.
Speed matters. Drive slower and the whole tune drops in pitch and stretches out. The tune was designed for 55 miles per hour, which is also the posted speed limit.
